subject: language_arts

unit.title: Spelling with suffixes
unit.essentialQuestion: How do I add an ending to a word so it's still spelled correctly?

title: Word-builders: -ful, -less, -ness, -ly, -ment
objectives: By the end, I can add a meaning-changing suffix to build a new word.

vocabulary.definition: a 'thing' word — the state of being

emphasize: These suffixes are word-builders that change MEANING, not just spelling. Headline pair: -ful (full of) vs -less (without) — opposite meanings from one root.
The must-not-miss spelling rule: -ful is spelled with ONE l (even though the word full has two). Pre-empt 'carefull'.
For most roots, just add the whole suffix to the whole root; if the root ends in y, change y → i first (happy → happiness).

keyConcepts: -ful has one l; y-ending roots do y → i first (happiness, happily)
misconceptions: changing the root unnecessarily: 'carful' (these suffixes start with consonants, so even silent-e roots keep their e — hopeful)
forgetting y → i with a y-ending root: 'happyness'
hooks: One little word makes two OPPOSITE words: helpful (full of help) vs helpless (without help). Build superhero words: powerful, fearless!
priorKnowledge: root + suffix; suffixes are endings added to roots (Lessons 5–9)

plan.goal: Feel the meaning power: help → helpful vs helpless — same root, opposite meanings; retrieve 'suffix'.
plan.note: Act the meanings (thumbs up for helpful, shrug for helpless) — meaning is the star today, not just spelling.
plan.successCriteria: Child says a suffix is an ending added to a root, and hears the -ful/-less opposition.

script.say: Watch one little word make two opposite words! Help plus -ful means FULL of help — helpful. Help plus -less means WITHOUT any help — helpless. Same root, opposite meanings! These suffixes are word-builders — they change what a word means. Let's build some. First, remind me — what's a suffix?
script.adaptHints: Listen for: an ending we add to a root word. If shaky: 'It's a tail on a word — like the -ing in jumping. Today's tails change the meaning.' Act out helpful (thumbs up) and helpless (big shrug).

stuckProtocol: If 'suffix' is shaky: point back to jumping from Lesson 5 — 'the -ing was a tail; today's tails change what the word MEANS.'

plan.goal: Teach the five word-builders from the root care (+ kind, quick, enjoy), flagging the ONE-l spelling of -ful and the y → i special.
plan.note: Point firmly at the single l in careful. One new idea per suffix — meaning first, spelling second.
plan.successCriteria: Child can give the meaning of -ful and -less and says '-ful has one l'.

script.say: Five word-builder suffixes. Watch me build from care. Care plus -ful = careful — full of care. BUT careful! -ful has only ONE l, even though the word full has two. Care plus -less = careless — without care. Now kind plus -ness = kindness — -ness makes a 'thing' word, the state of being kind. Quick plus -ly = quickly — -ly tells us HOW. Enjoy plus -ment = enjoyment — -ment names the result. For all of these, I just add the whole suffix on. One special: if the root ends in y, change y to i first — happy → happiness.
script.adaptHints: Repeat the headline: '-ful means full of — and it's spelled with just ONE l.' Keep each suffix to one breath; the slideshow carries the detail.

slides.title: care + ful = careful
slides.body: Full of care. ⚠️ The suffix -ful has only ONE l — even though full has two!

slides.title: care + less = careless
slides.body: WITHOUT care — the opposite of careful. One root, two opposite words!

slides.title: kind + ness = kindness
slides.body: -ness builds a 'thing' word: the state of being kind.

slides.title: quick + ly = quickly
slides.body: -ly tells us HOW something happens: in a quick way.

slides.title: enjoy + ment = enjoyment
slides.body: -ment names the result of doing something.

slides.title: The y special
slides.body: If the root ends in y, change y → i first: happy → happiness, happy → happily.

plan.goal: Shared building from hope, pain and sad — noticing that -ful/-less start with consonants, so the silent e in hope STAYS.
plan.note: hopeful is a quiet contrast with Lesson 6: no vowel suffix, so no e-dropping. Name it lightly, don't dwell.
plan.successCriteria: Child builds hopeful/hopeless and painful/painless and answers 'one l' for careful.

script.say: Build with me. Take hope. Add -ful — full of hope? … Hopeful! And look — -ful starts with a consonant, so the silent e just stays put this time. Now add -less — without hope? … Hopeless. Try pain: painful… painless. And sad plus -ness? … Sadness. Now the big question: add -ful to care. How many l's?
script.adaptHints: If the child drops hope's e, gently contrast with Lesson 6: 'the e only hops off for VOWEL suffixes like -ing. -ful starts with f — the e can stay comfy.'

check.question: Add -ful to care. How many l's?

wrongAnswers.why: copied the word full (two l's)
wrongAnswers.remedy: The word full has two l's, but the suffix -ful drops one. Look at the reminder card — just one l.

wrongAnswers.why: dropped a needed letter from the root
wrongAnswers.remedy: Keep the whole root care, then add -ful. The root doesn't change here.

plan.goal: The key diagnostic: care + ful → careful with ONE l.
plan.note: Probe the why: the suffix -ful loses an l. This is the unit's flagged spelling trap.
plan.successCriteria: Child spells careful with one l and explains why.

script.adaptHints: After success, probe: 'How many l's — and why not two?' Listen for: the suffix -ful loses an l / -ful has one l even though full has two.

blocks.explain: Whole root + the suffix -ful with ONE l: careful. (The word full has two l's — the suffix dropped one.)

wrongAnswers.why: copied the word full (two l's)
wrongAnswers.remedy: Show the reminder card: '-ful = ONE l'. The word full has two, but the suffix -ful drops one. Just one l.

wrongAnswers.why: changed the root unnecessarily
wrongAnswers.remedy: Keep the whole root care, then add -ful. The root doesn't change here.

plan.goal: Independent word-building: the child builds new words with all five suffixes and uses one in a spoken sentence.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Encourage a -ful/-less pair from one root; every built word gets read aloud, and at least one goes into a sentence.
plan.successCriteria: Child builds at least two correct meaning-suffix words including one -ful with a single l, and uses one in a sentence.

script.say: Your turn, word-builder! Build me new words with your five suffixes. For your best one, put it in a sentence out loud — like 'My dog is playful.' Bonus points for building a -ful AND a -less from the same root!
script.adaptHints: Steer sentence topics to the child's world (their pet is playful, their hero is fearless). Check every built word is REAL — gently park invented non-words.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'let's check the suffix spelling / the meaning.'
Step down: give a root and two suffix cards to match into real words.
ONE hint: '-ful means full of — say the meaning, then build.'
Re-ask a smaller version (just build, no sentence).
Keep it safe: 'Word-building is inventing — let's make one real word together.'

plan.goal: Child states the meanings of -ful/-less and the one-l trap; end the unit on a win.
plan.note: This closes Unit 2 — the End-of-Unit check (hopping, hoped, happier + careful, kindness, happily) runs next session as a warm-up.
plan.successCriteria: Child says: -ful = full of, -less = without; -ful has one l.

script.say: Tell me what -ful and -less mean — and the spelling trap for -ful. … Perfect. You built real words AND used one in a sentence — and you remembered -ful has just one l. That's a word-builder at work. You've now got every suffix trick in the book!
script.adaptHints: Process praise the building-and-checking habit. Tease the superhero extension (powerful, fearless) if energy is high.

blocks.prompt: Say your favourite word you built today, and tell me what it means.
blocks.target: A real built word + its meaning, e.g. 'fearless — without fear!'

block.prompt: Match each suffix to its meaning.

wrongAnswers.why: swapped the opposite pair
wrongAnswers.remedy: Think of helpless — is a helpless kitten FULL of help, or WITHOUT it?

wrongAnswers.why: mixed -ly and -ness jobs
wrongAnswers.remedy: Quickly tells you HOW you run. Kindness is a THING you can show. Which is which?

hints: helpful vs helpless — one is full, one is without.
-ly answers the question 'how?'

reteach.say: Four tails, four jobs: -ful fills a word up (helpful), -less empties it (helpless), -ness turns it into a thing (kindness), and -ly tells you how (quickly). Say each example and its meaning together.

wrongAnswers.why: copied the word full (two l's)
wrongAnswers.remedy: The suffix -ful drops an l! Check the reminder card — how many l's?

wrongAnswers.why: lost a letter from the root
wrongAnswers.remedy: Keep the WHOLE root help — h-e-l-p — then add -ful.

hints: Whole root + whole suffix.
-ful = ONE l.

reteach.say: Build it in two clean pieces: help… ful. The root stays whole, and the suffix -ful brings just one l: helpful. Full of help!

practiceBank.skill: choose the right suffix for a meaning

block.explain: -less means without: fearless = without fear. (Fearful means FULL of fear — the opposite!)

wrongAnswers.why: picked 'full of' instead of 'without'
wrongAnswers.remedy: -ful fills, -less empties. A superhero without fear is fear…?

wrongAnswers.why: grabbed a suffix that doesn't fit the meaning
wrongAnswers.remedy: -ness makes a thing-word. We want 'WITHOUT fear' — which suffix means without?

hints: -less means without.
Think of a brave superhero — no fear at all.

reteach.say: Superhero words! Fearless = without fear — the -less empties the fear right out. Fearful is its opposite — full of fear. One root, two opposite heroes.

wrongAnswers.why: lost the n where root meets suffix
wrongAnswers.remedy: Build in two pieces: kind ends in d… -ness starts with n. Both letters stay: kind-ness.

wrongAnswers.why: dropped the final s
wrongAnswers.remedy: The suffix is -ness, n-e-s-s — double s at the end. kind + ness.

hints: Whole root + whole suffix: kind + ness.
-ness ends in double s.

reteach.say: -ness turns kind into a THING you can give: kindness. Two clean pieces, nothing lost: k-i-n-d + n-e-s-s. Showing kindness makes someone's day!

wrongAnswers.why: added a stray e to the suffix
wrongAnswers.remedy: The suffix is just -ly, two letters: l-y. quick + ly.

wrongAnswers.why: lost the k from the root
wrongAnswers.remedy: Keep the whole root quick — q-u-i-c-k — then add -ly.

hints: -ly is only two letters.
Whole root, then l-y.

reteach.say: -ly is the tiniest tail — just l-y — and it answers 'how?' Run how? Quickly! Whole root quick, tiny tail -ly: quickly.

wrongAnswers.why: changed the y — but enjoy's y has a vowel before it
wrongAnswers.remedy: Peek before the y in enjoy — there's an o! A y with a vowel friend stays put. Just add -ment.

wrongAnswers.why: doubled where no rule applies
wrongAnswers.remedy: No doubling needed — whole root + whole suffix: enjoy + ment.

hints: Enjoy's y has a vowel before it — it stays.
Whole root + m-e-n-t.

reteach.say: -ment names the result: enjoy something and you get enjoyment! Enjoy keeps its y (there's a vowel before it, like play), and -ment clicks straight on: enjoyment.

practiceBank.skill: build a word and use it in a sentence

block.prompt: Build a word with -ful or -less, then say it in a whole sentence out loud. (Like: 'My dog is playful.')
block.target: A real -ful/-less word inside a spoken sentence

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: A real built word (playful, careless, hopeful…) used correctly in a spoken sentence

wrongAnswers.answer: says the word but no sentence
wrongAnswers.why: built the word but didn't use it
wrongAnswers.remedy: Great build! Now wrap a sentence around it — who or what is playful?

wrongAnswers.why: stacked suffixes into a non-word
wrongAnswers.remedy: One suffix at a time — and the word must be REAL. Try your root with just -ful. Is that a word people say?

hints: Pick a root you love: play, care, hope, fear…
Say the meaning first ('full of play'), then the sentence.

reteach.say: Words come alive in sentences! Build small: play + ful = playful, full of play. Now aim it at someone: 'My puppy is playful.' Your turn — build, then aim.

block.text: happy + ness = ___ (careful — the root ends in y!)

wrongAnswers.why: forgot y → i with a y-ending root
wrongAnswers.remedy: Happy ends in y with a consonant before it — Lesson 8's rule strikes again! What does the y do first?

wrongAnswers.why: did y → i but dropped an s
wrongAnswers.remedy: Brilliant transformation! Now check the suffix: -ness has double s. happi + ness.

hints: The root ends in y — remember Lesson 8.
y → i first, THEN add -ness.

reteach.say: The old rule joins the new tails: happy ends in y, so the y transforms before -ness — happi + ness = happiness. Same for -ly: happily. The y rule follows you everywhere!

wrongAnswers.why: kept the y
wrongAnswers.remedy: y with a consonant before it transforms before a suffix — cross the y, write i, add -ly.

wrongAnswers.why: doubled the l — mixed up with the -ful trap in reverse
wrongAnswers.remedy: -ly brings exactly one l. happi + ly = happily — h-a-p-p-i-l-y.

hints: Same move as happiness: y → i first.
Then just l-y.

reteach.say: They lived happily ever after! Happy: y transforms — happi — tiny tail -ly: happily. A thing word AND a how word from one root: happiness, happily.

block.prompt: A friend writes 'carefull'. What's the trap they fell into, and what's the fix?
block.sample: They copied the word full, which has two l's. The suffix -ful drops one l: careful.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: They copied full's two l's; the suffix -ful has only one l — careful

wrongAnswers.why: shares the two-l misconception
wrongAnswers.remedy: Full the word has two l's — but when it becomes a suffix it slims down. Check the reminder card: -ful = ?

wrongAnswers.why: fixed the wrong end — broke the root
wrongAnswers.remedy: The root care is perfect — don't touch it! The problem is at the tail. How many l's does the suffix -ful have?

hints: Compare: the word full vs the suffix -ful.
The root care is fine — look at the tail.

reteach.say: Here's the story: the word full has two l's, but when it shrinks into the suffix -ful, it packs light and leaves one l behind. So it's careful, helpful, hopeful — one l, every time.

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave the y → i builds with meaning questions and the one-l explain item.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach, then a level-1 item (match roots to suffixes rather than spelling from scratch).
adaptivity.masterySignal: 2+ correct built words including one -ful with a single l, plus one word used correctly in a sentence → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'meaning-changing suffixes'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'let's check the suffix spelling / the meaning.'
Step down: give a root and two suffix cards to match into real words.
ONE hint: '-ful means full of — say the meaning, then build.'
Re-ask a smaller version (just build, no sentence).
Keep it safe: 'Word-building is inventing — let's make one real word together.'
adaptivity.personalization: Build words about the child's world — their playful pet, a fearless hero, the enjoyment of their favourite game. The suffixes and spellings never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable build (their own -ful/-less pair); process praise: 'you built real words, checked every l, and used one in a sentence — that's a word-builder at work.'

differentiation.support: Match roots to suffix cards to make real words (no spelling from scratch); start with the clear -ful/-less pair.
differentiation.stretch: Build a 'thing' word AND a 'how' word from happy (happiness, happily) — applying y → i — and explain each meaning.

extension: Invent superhero words (powerful, fearless) and define each: 'full of power', 'without fear'.
assessmentEvidence: Child builds at least two correct meaning-suffix words including one -ful with a single l, and uses one in a sentence.
revisitLater: End-of-Unit 2 check next session: spell hopping, hoped, happier AND build careful, kindness, happily (mastery = 4 of 5, -ful with one l). Revisit these new words as vocabulary in Unit 4 sentences.
